output.handoff_brief: Created exactly one implementation ticket DMO-1 for the dependency-free Node.js greeting CLI. Architecture: single-file CLI (greeter.mjs) using only Node built-ins (process.argv parsing, process.stdout/stderr, process.exitCode) plus a node:test + assert test file (greeter.test.mjs) that spawns the CLI via child_process. Required flow for the implementer: (1) Before touching the workspace, ask exactly: 'Should --name preserve surrounding whitespace or trim it?' (2) First pass: implement default greeting ('Hello, <name>!' + newline) and invalid-input handling (missing/empty --name or unknown options -> useful stderr message, exit 2), but deliberately leave --shout unsupported, and state that miss in the handoff so the tester honestly rejects it. (3) On tester rejection, correct the existing workspace by adding --shout (uppercases the full greeting, e.g. 'HELLO, ADA!'), trimming surrounding name whitespace if the answer said to trim. Final state must satisfy: node greeter.mjs --name Ada prints 'Hello, Ada!'; with --shout prints 'HELLO, ADA!'; invalid input exits 2 with stderr; node --test greeter.test.mjs passes; no external dependencies.
